mainTopic: בְּרֵירָה (deciding later which item was meant all along) in רבי יהודה's view: it does not work when it depends on a person's own decision, but it does work when it depends on something outside his control. רב משרשיא then challenges this.
overview: This amud finishes a proof that רבי יהודה rejects בְּרֵירָה when a person makes something depend on his own later choice. The proof is the case of wine bought from כותים, where רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid drinking right away, while רבי מאיר permits it. The גמרא then quotes a משנה about a sick husband's conditional גט. There רבי יהודה says the גט takes effect when he dies, which shows he accepts בְּרֵירָה when the outcome depends on something outside the person's control. רב משרשיא then points out to רבא that רבי שמעון holds the very same split. The גמרא proves the first half from the wine case. It proves the second half from a ברייתא about betrothal made conditional on the father's wish. That ברייתא, and the point of רב משרשיא's challenge, continue on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the wine case: רבי מאיר permits drinking, the others forbid
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about wine bought from כותים ends. רבי מאיר lets the buyer redeem the מעשר שני and drink right away. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And he redeems the מעשר שני and drinks right away. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote that proves רבי יהודה does not accept בְּרֵירָה when a person makes something depend on his own future choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer says now that the portions he will separate later are תרומה and מעשר. רבי מאיר says his later choice shows retroactively which wine was holy all along, so he may drink now. רבי יהודה forbids it. That means he holds there is no בְּרֵירָה when the choice is the person's own.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeems: transfers the holiness of מעשר שני onto money
They forbid
Retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was meant from the start
The second tithe, which must be eaten in ירושלים or redeemed

steps.confusionAlert: The buyer has not separated anything yet. The whole question is whether a choice he makes later can count as if it had been made from the beginning.

phrases.english: and he redeems [the second tithe] and drinks immediately,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹסְרִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon forbid it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵיחֵל וְשׁוֹתֶה מִיָּד, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the source the גמרא began quoting before this section.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה holds there is no בְּרֵירָה when a person makes something depend on his own decision.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about wine bought from כותים, where רבי יהודה forbids drinking right away.

steps.title: When it depends on others, רבי יהודה accepts בְּרֵירָה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא claims that when the outcome depends on others, רבי יהודה does accept בְּרֵירָה. It begins quoting a משנה to prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: "When a person makes something depend on the decision of others, he holds of בְּרֵירָה. As we learned in a משנה: What is her status during those days?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the second half of רבי יהודה's view and starts quoting a משנה as its source. This line is setting up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we have a split in רבי יהודה's view. When the outcome depends on his own choice, there is no בְּרֵירָה. When it depends on others, there is בְּרֵירָה. The משנה being quoted is about a sick husband who gives a גט that works 'from now, if I die.' It asks about the wife's status before he dies.

keyTerms.meaning: Making something depend on the decision of others, not oneself
He holds of / accepts
As we learned in a משנה
During those days: between the giving of the גט and the husband's death

phrases.english: [when one] makes it depend on the decision of others,
he holds of retroactive clarification,
as we learned in a mishna:
What is she during those days?
phrases.notes: This is from a משנה later in גיטין about a sick man who gives a גט 'from now, if I die.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת אֲחֵרִים אִית לֵיהּ בְּרֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the opposite half of רבי יהודה's view after step 1 proved the first half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, בְּרֵירָה works when the outcome depends on others.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: when he dies, it is a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that the woman is fully married until the husband dies. Once he dies, the גט takes effect. This shows he accepts בְּרֵירָה here.
steps.simpleTranslation: "רבי יהודה says: She is like a married woman in every way. When he dies, it is a גט."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. In the משנה, רבי יהודה says the גט works once the husband dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט cannot start working after the husband is already dead. So if it works at all, it must work retroactively, from the time it was given. Whether he dies is not his own choice, so it counts like 'depending on others.' This proves רבי יהודה accepts בְּרֵירָה in that kind of case.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a married woman
In all her matters (fully)
And when he dies
A bill of divorce (גט)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's view has two sides. When something depends on the person's own choice, there is no בְּרֵירָה (the wine case). When it depends on others or on events outside his control, there is בְּרֵירָה (the sick husband's גט).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ לְכׇל דְּבָרֶיהָ,
phrases.english: she is like a married woman in all her matters,
and when he dies, it is a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ לְכׇל דְּבָרֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the answer from the משנה that step 2 began quoting.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה accepts בְּרֵירָה when the outcome depends on others.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (גיטין 73a) where רבי יהודה rules that the sick husband's גט takes effect when he dies.

steps.title: רב משרשיא: רבי שמעון holds the same split
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא points out to רבא that רבי שמעון holds the very same two-sided view as רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "רב משרשיא said to רבא: But רבי שמעון also holds there is no בְּרֵירָה when it depends on his own decision, and there is בְּרֵירָה when it depends on others!"
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא raises a challenge to רבא. The split just shown for רבי יהודה is also true of רבי שמעון. This opens a new question the גמרא will deal with next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון also forbade drinking in the wine case, so he too rejects בְּרֵירָה when it depends on one's own decision. רב משרשיא adds that רבי שמעון accepts בְּרֵירָה when it depends on others. The next two steps prove both halves, and the full force of his challenge comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who questions רבא here
Making something depend on one's own decision
He does not hold of
But look at / isn't there

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said to Rava:
But there is Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת עַצְמוֹ לֵית לֵיהּ בְּרֵירָה,
phrases.english: who, where one makes it depend on his own decision, does not hold of retroactive clarification,
phrases.notes: We saw this in step 1, where רבי שמעון forbade drinking the wine.

phrases.aramaic: וְתוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת אֲחֵרִים אִית לֵיהּ בְּרֵירָה!
phrases.english: and where one makes it depend on the decision of others, does hold of retroactive clarification!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא לְרָבָא: הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the split just proven for רבי יהודה and shows that רבי שמעון holds it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way רבא presented the discussion, built around רבי יהודה's split view on בְּרֵירָה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון holds the identical distinction between depending on one's own decision and depending on others. רב משרשיא raises this as a challenge, and its point is developed after the proofs, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי שמעון rejects retroactive clarification when it depends on one's own choice
steps.stepSummary: The first half of רבי שמעון's view: when the outcome hangs on one's own decision, he does not accept בְּרֵירָה. The source is the wine case already discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a person makes it depend on his own decision, רבי שמעון does not accept בְּרֵירָה. We know this from what we said earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now backs up רב משרשיא's claim that רבי שמעון holds the same two-sided view as רבי יהודה. It starts with the side where the outcome depends on the person himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the wine case from the ברייתא, רבי שמעון forbade drinking right away. That shows he does not trust a later choice to decide what was true from the start. That choice was the buyer's own, so this proves רבי שמעון rejects בְּרֵירָה when it depends on one's own decision.

keyTerms.meaning: Making the outcome depend on his own decision
Retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was true from the start
That which we already said

phrases.english: One who makes it depend on his own decision
he (Rabbi Shimon) does not accept retroactive clarification
as we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to the wine bought from כותים, where רבי שמעון did not let the buyer drink right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת עַצְמוֹ לֵית לֵיהּ בְּרֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the first half of רב משרשיא's claim from Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון rejects בְּרֵירָה when the outcome depends on one's own decision.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about wine bought from כותים (Step 1).

steps.title: רבי שמעון accepts retroactive clarification when it depends on another person
steps.stepSummary: The second half of רבי שמעון's view: when the outcome hangs on someone else's decision, he accepts בְּרֵירָה. The proof is a ברייתא about betrothal made conditional on the father's wish.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a person makes it depend on someone else's decision, רבי שמעון accepts בְּרֵירָה, as a ברייתא teaches: If a man says, "I am betrothing you through relations on the condition that my father will want it," she is betrothed even if the father did not want it. רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: If the father wants it, she is betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove the second half: רבי שמעון accepts בְּרֵירָה when the outcome depends on another person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי שמעון's view, whether the betrothal works depends on what the father wants. His later wish reveals whether she was betrothed from the start, which is בְּרֵירָה. The father is someone else, so this shows רבי שמעון accepts בְּרֵירָה in that kind of case, exactly like רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Making the outcome depend on someone else's decision
I am having relations with you (for the purpose of betrothal)
On the condition that
She is betrothed

steps.whyThisMatters: With both halves shown, רבי שמעון turns out to match רבי יהודה's view. That sets up the challenge רב משרשיא is building toward.

phrases.english: One who makes it depend on the decision of others
he (רבי שמעון) accepts retroactive clarification
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
"I am having relations with you (for betrothal)
on the condition that my father will want it";

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה הָאָב –
phrases.english: even if the father did not want it,
she is betrothed.
רבי שמעון בן יהודה says
in the name of רבי שמעון:
If the father wants it, she is betrothed,

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת אֲחֵרִים אִית לֵיהּ בְּרֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of רב משרשיא's two-sided claim about רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון accepts בְּרֵירָה when the outcome depends on another person's decision.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about betrothal conditioned on the father's wish, cited by רבי שמעון בן יהודה in the name of רבי שמעון.
